\section{Background}

\subsection{Alignment and costs}

Let \(A=a_1\dots a_n\) be the reference and \(B=b_1\dots b_m\) the query, and let cell \((i,j)\) lie on diagonal \(j-i\). Under gap-affine costs \((x, o, e)\), for example (4, 6, 2), a match costs 0, a mismatch \(x\) and a gap of \(k\) letters \(g(k)=o+ke\); unit costs have \(x=e=1\) and \(o=0\), two-piece costs take the minimum of two such functions \citep{Li2018minimap2}, and a substitution matrix scores each pair of letters. Besides global alignment, dinara-align offers ends-free, extension \citep{Li2018minimap2} and local alignment, the last two maximising a score that rewards matches (Section 3.8). An alignment is \emph{optimal} if none has a lower cost, or a higher score, under the requested costs and mode, within any band or cost limit the caller sets; an exact aligner returns one or reports that none exists. At unit costs the distance \(D(i,j)\) between the prefixes \(a_1\dots a_i\) and \(b_1\dots b_j\) satisfies

\begin{equation}\begin{gathered}
D(i,j) = \min\bigl(D(i-1,j)+1,\; D(i,j-1)+1,\\ D(i-1,j-1)+[a_i \ne b_j]\bigr),
\end{gathered}\end{equation}

where \([a_i \ne b_j]\) is 1 if the letters differ and 0 otherwise, with \(D(i,0)=i\) and \(D(0,j)=j\), and the distance is \(D(n,m)\); gap-affine costs need three such layers \citep{Gotoh1982}.

\subsection{Band doubling and bit-parallel computation}

At unit costs, an alignment of cost at most \(t\) visits only diagonals \(d\) with \(|d| + |d - \delta| \le t\), where \(\delta = m - n\); band doubling computes only those cells, doubling \(t\) until \(D(n,m) \le t\) \citep{Ukkonen1985}. Myers' recurrence advances the score differences of 64 cells of a column, held in two machine words, by one column at a time \citep{Myers1999bitvector}, and A*PA2 computes the band in tiles of 256 columns with SIMD vectors \citep{GrootKoerkamp2024astarpa2}.

\subsection{Diagonal transition}

Diagonal transition keeps, for each cost \(s\) and diagonal, the furthest cell an alignment of cost \(s\) reaches, extended along matches at no cost, in \(O(ns)\) time in the worst case and \(O(n + s^2)\) expected time on random sequences \citep{Ukkonen1985,Myers1986ond}; WFA generalises it to gap-affine costs, where the wavefront, or front, of each cost has three layers \citep{MarcoSola2021wfa}, and BiWFA runs it from both ends \citep{MarcoSola2023biwfa}.

\subsection{The seed heuristic}

A*PA divides the reference into disjoint seeds and finds their matches in the query, exactly or with one edit \citep{GrootKoerkamp2024astarpa}. A seed crossed unmatched costs its potential \(r\), 1 for exact seeds and 2 for inexact ones. The gap-chaining seed heuristic charges a chain of matches the cost of each match and, for each gap between consecutive matches and to the end, the larger of the potential of the seeds it spans and the number of diagonals it shifts; its least charge never exceeds the remaining cost, and A*PA keeps the match starts in layers by the potential their best chain saves. A*PA2 prunes matches before the alignment: a match \(\nu\) of cost \(c(\nu)\) is kept only if a path from its end, starting at cost \(c(\nu)\), crosses the next \(p = 14\) seeds while its cost stays below their potential \citep{GrootKoerkamp2024astarpa2}, which a diagonal transition from the match's end tests, dropping each furthest point whose cost reaches that potential. A*PA2 then drops the rows of each band whose score plus the heuristic exceeds the bound.
